_comment: Collector instances this machine may query, and the credential for each. Copy to remote_endpoints.json and fill in. The collector itself never reads this file - it does not know it exists. One program does: `python -m python.main watch`, this project's own status shell, which takes the base_url and token of the entry named by --endpoint (default: watch). For everything else it is a note to whoever is working here, machine-readable so a session does not have to be told the URL again.
_naming: Entries here are named after WHAT THEY REACH and with what rights. 'watch' is this repository's own shell - it has nothing to do with the FiniexViewer project, which is a separate peer with its own credentials. The consumer name on the box should say the same thing: 'collector_watch', never 'viewer'.
_rules: The real file is gitignored. It never becomes tracked, never reaches the bus, never gets pasted into an issue.
One token per consumer, so revoking one does not disturb the others. This one is the operator's; the consuming project has its own; the status shell has its own.
The token authorises exactly the grants listed beside it. If a route answers 403, the grant is missing - it is not a bug in the route.
Print the URL freely, never the token. A command that needs it reads it from here.

watch.token: <40 characters, generated on the box, its own>
watch.note: What `python -m python.main watch` uses by default. status:detail and nothing else: this shell sits open on a desk all day, and a token that can also fetch archive files is a credential left lying in a window.

watch_local.token: <the same collector_watch token, on the box itself>
watch_local.note: The same shell against a collector on this machine. Loopback, so it reads once a second instead of once every two.

live.instance_id: <minted at the data root on first start; /v1/status states it>
live.note: The operator's own credential, for diagnostics from a session - archive listings, log excerpts, file transfers. Not what the status shell should be pointed at.
